title_en: Guangxi Guiguan Electric Power Co., Ltd. v. Guangxi Yongchen Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. — dispute over house sale contract
ruling_gist_en: Article 97 of the Contract Law of the PRC provides: "After rescission of a contract, performance that has not yet been rendered shall be terminated; for performance that has already been rendered, depending on the circumstances of performance and the nature of the contract, the parties may request restoration to the original status quo, adopt other remedial measures, and have the right to claim damages." Rescission of a contract extinguishes the contractual relationship. Therefore, the legal consequence of rescission is not liability for breach of contract, but rather civil liability in the form of restitution of unjust enrichment, compensation for losses, and the like.

full_text_en:
Guangxi Guiguan Electric Power Co., Ltd. v. Guangxi Yongcheng Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. — dispute over house sales contract

[Ruling Summary]

Article 97 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "After a contract is terminated, for the part not yet performed, performance shall be discharged; for the part already performed, based on the circumstances of performance and the nature of the contract, the parties may request restoration to the original status or adopt other remedial measures, and have the right to claim damages." The termination of a contract causes the contractual relationship to be extinguished; therefore, the legal consequences of contract termination are not manifested as liability for breach of contract, but as civil liability in the form of restitution of unjust enrichment, compensation for losses, and the like.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2009) Min Yi Zhong Zi No. 23

Appellant (Defendant at First Instance): Guangxi Yongcheng Real Estate Development Co., Ltd., domiciled at Room 301, Unit 2, Building D, Lingnan Jiayuan, No. 135 Dongge Road, Nanning City, Guangxi.

Legal Representative: Cheng Haiyu, Chairman of the Board.

Agent ad litem: Liu Zhihong, lawyer of Beijing Shanggong Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Ouyang Zeming, lawyer of Guangtianyi Law Firm.

Respondent (Plaintiff at First Instance): Guangxi Guiguan Electric Power Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 6, Beisi Li, Minzhu Road, Nanning City, Guangxi.

Legal Representative: Yang Qing, Chairman of the Board.

Agent ad litem: Zhang Jie, lawyer of Beijing Weiheng Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Wei Xiumin, lawyer of Beijing Weiheng Law Firm.

With respect to the dispute over house sales contract between the appellant Guangxi Yongcheng Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Yongcheng Company) and the respondent Guangxi Guiguan Electric Power Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Guiguan Company), the High People's Court of Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region rendered a civil judgment (2007) Gui Min Yi Chu Zi No. 2 on December 25, 2008. Dissatisfied with this judgment, Yongcheng Company appealed to this Court. This Court lawfully formed a collegial panel and held a court session on May 26, 2009. The agents ad litem of Yongcheng Company, Liu Zhihong and Ouyang Zeming, and the agents ad litem of Guiguan Company, Zhang Jie and Wei Xiumin, appeared before the court to participate in the proceedings. The case is now concluded.

The court of first instance found the following facts upon trial:

On March 12, 2003, Guiguan Company (Party A) and Yongcheng Company (Party B) entered into the "Agreement on Directed Development and Construction of Base" (hereinafter referred to as the "Directed Development Agreement"), entrusting Yongcheng Company to construct an office complex and a commercial residential community for Guiguan Company at the Langdong Fengling Section, Nanning City, Guangxi. The agreement stipulated: The main office building was initially set at 21 floors, covering an area of approximately 30 mu, with a gross floor area of approximately 30,000 square meters. The total investment in the office building included: land at RMB 530,000 per mu (including land leveling fees); construction and development cost provisionally calculated at RMB 2,500 per square meter. The commercial residential community was a 6-story frame structure, covering an area of approximately 30 mu, with a unit price calculated at RMB 1,500 per square meter. The parties also agreed on the establishment of a joint account, payment methods, contract duration, guarantee obligations, other rights and obligations of both parties, and liability for breach of contract. After the agreement was signed, Guiguan Company paid Yongcheng Company RMB 500,000, RMB 19,500,000, and RMB 5,900,000 on April 16, 2003, October 17, 2003, and November 15, 2004, respectively, totaling RMB 25,900,000. On July 8, 2003, Yongcheng Company obtained the "Land Use Planning Permit" issued by Nanning City Planning Administration Bureau. On February 5, 2005, Yongcheng Company completed the bidding for earth excavation, pile foundation, and foundation pit support for Building 1-3# Comprehensive Building, Zone A of Fortune International Plaza, Fengling Commercial Residential Community. On March 28, 2005, Yongcheng Company obtained the "Construction Work Construction Permit" for the foundation of Building 1-3# Comprehensive Building, Zone A of Fortune International Plaza, Fengling Commercial Residential Community.

On March 30, 2005, Guiguan Company (Party A) and Yongcheng Company (Party B) entered into the "Supplementary Agreement on Directed Development and Construction of Base for Guangxi Guiguan Electric Power Co., Ltd." (hereinafter referred to as the "Supplementary Agreement"), stipulating that the main office building was initially set at 26 floors, with a gross floor area of 45,955 square meters. The land compensation fee for the office building was RMB 950,000 per mu, totaling RMB 28,500,000, and the land leveling fee was RMB 2,000,000. The basic development and construction cost was RMB 4,350 per square meter, totaling RMB 199,904,250. Regarding payment methods, the parties agreed that the fees paid by Guiguan Company before March 30, 2005, would be treated as the portion already paid for land compensation. Within five working days after the signing of this Supplementary Agreement, Guiguan Company would pay the remaining land compensation fee. Within ten working days after the completion of the site leveling work, Guiguan Company would pay Yongcheng Company RMB 2,000,000. Within seven days after Yongcheng Company obtained the construction permit for the office building, Guiguan Company would pay 25% of the basic development and construction cost, approximately RMB 50,000,000. After deducting the initial payment of RMB 20,000,000, the actual project prepayment was RMB 30,000,000. The method for disbursing interim payments based on physical progress: Within seven days after the completion of the pile foundation work for the office building, Guiguan Company would pay 5% of the basic development and construction cost, i.e., RMB 10,000,000, to Yongcheng Company; within seven days after the completion of the basement work for the office building, Guiguan Company would pay 10% of the basic development and construction cost, i.e., RMB 20,000,000, to Yongcheng Company; within seven days after the completion of the fourth-floor slab structure of the office building, Guiguan Company would pay 10% of the basic development and construction cost, i.e., RMB 20,000,000, to Yongcheng Company; within seven days after the completion of the eighth-floor slab structure of the office building, Guiguan Company would pay 10% of the basic development and construction cost, i.e., RMB 20,000,000, to Yongcheng Company... The parties agreed on the work schedule: After this Supplementary Agreement takes effect, Yongcheng Company would provide the planning site map and the "Land Use Planning Permit" within 15 working days, and obtain the "State-owned Land Use Right Certificate" within 30 working days; after the construction design drawings were approved, Yongcheng Company would complete the supervision and construction bidding within June 2005; after the construction bidding, Yongcheng Company would obtain the construction permit for the office building within July 2005; in August 2005, the pile foundation work for the office building would be completed; in December 2005, the basement work for the office building would be completed; in February 2006, the fourth-floor slab structure of the office building would be completed... Within 6 months from the start of the main structure construction of the office building, Yongcheng Company would obtain the commercial housing pre-sale permit for the office building, enter into a commercial housing pre-sale contract with Guiguan Company, and file with the real estate bureau; within 28 months from the start of the main structure construction of the office building, Yongcheng Company would complete the completion and acceptance inspection, and within 2 months after passing the inspection, deliver the office building to Guiguan Company for use. In terms of rights and obligations, the parties agreed: Guiguan Company had the right to supervise the project progress; if the physical progress did not meet the scheduled requirements, Guiguan Company had the right to refuse payment of any amount. Regarding delivery, the parties agreed: If Yongcheng Company was unable to deliver on time, Guiguan Company could choose to notify Yongcheng Company to terminate the agreement or continue waiting. If Guiguan Company chose to continue waiting, the waiting period would be determined by Guiguan Company; after waiting, it could still terminate the agreement. Yongcheng Company guaranteed that, before Guiguan Company obtained the "Nanning City House Ownership Certificate," without Guiguan Company's consent, Yongcheng Company would not mortgage the land use right to a third party in any form. Regarding liability for breach of contract, the parties agreed: Guiguan Company must pay the project funds to Yongcheng Company in accordance with the time and construction progress specified in this Supplementary Agreement; if payment was overdue, Guiguan Company would pay Yongcheng Company liquidated damages at a rate of 0.02% per day of the overdue amount. If the delay exceeded 30 days, it would be deemed that Guiguan Company was unable to continue performing the agreement, and Yongcheng Company had the right to unilaterally terminate the agreement. If this Supplementary Agreement became invalid, could not be performed, or the land use right was mortgaged to a third party due to Yongcheng Company's development procedures or other reasons, Yongcheng Company must bear liability for breach of contract, return all development funds and interest to Guiguan Company, double return the deposit, and compensate for the economic losses caused to Guiguan Company. If Yongcheng Company failed to complete the relevant work within the time specified in the work schedule of this Supplementary Agreement, it would be deemed a breach of contract. For each overdue payment, Yongcheng Company would pay Guiguan Company liquidated damages at a rate of 0.02% per day of the amount received. If the delay exceeded 30 days, it would be deemed that Yongcheng Company was unable to continue performing the agreement, and Guiguan Company had the right to unilaterally terminate the agreement. If Yongcheng Company was unable to deliver the project on time as agreed, Guiguan Company had the right to require Yongcheng Company to pay liquidated damages on a daily basis, at a rate of 0.03% per day of the basic development and construction cost. If Yongcheng Company violated the land mortgage restriction, it must pay liquidated damages on a daily basis, at a rate of 0.03% per day of the basic development and construction cost, and compensate Guiguan Company for all losses arising therefrom. If Yongcheng Company was unable to timely obtain the "Nanning City House Ownership Certificate" and the right collateral certificate for the directed development and construction property, it must pay liquidated damages on a daily basis, at a rate of 0.03% per day of the basic development and construction cost, and compensate Guiguan Company for all losses arising therefrom: including bank loan interest, bank penalty interest, litigation costs, attorney fees, decoration costs, downtime costs, transportation costs, losses due to price increases from repurchase or reconstruction, etc. The parties agreed that after the signing of this Supplementary Agreement, the original agreement remained valid; in case of conflict between this Supplementary Agreement and the original agreement, the Supplementary Agreement shall prevail.

After the signing of the Supplementary Agreement, Guiguan Company paid Yongcheng Company RMB 54,600,000, RMB 10,000,000, and RMB 20,000,000 on April 12, 2005, August 9, 2006, and September 7, 2006, respectively. By then, Guiguan Company had paid a total of RMB 110,500,000 to Yongcheng Company for the construction of the office building. On January 4, 2006, Yongcheng Company completed the bidding for civil construction (including pile foundation), water and electricity lightning protection, air conditioning and ventilation, ventilation, fire protection and human defense. On April 6, 2006, the pile foundation work for the office building was completed. On May 25, 2006, Yongcheng Company obtained the "Construction Work Planning Permit" and its annex for Building 1# Office Building, Zone A, issued by Nanning City Planning Administration Bureau. On June 21, 2006, Yongcheng Company obtained the "Construction Work Construction Permit" for Fortune International Plaza Zone A, B, C projects of Fengling Commercial Residential Community (Phase II), issued by Nanning City Construction Committee. On August 16, 2006, Yongcheng Company completed the basement work for the office building. On December 5, 2006, Yongcheng Company completed the fourth-floor slab structure work for the office building. On December 9, 2006, China Construction Corporation, the contractor of the Fortune International Plaza project, sent a letter to Yongcheng Company, stating that due to Yongcheng Company's long-term arrears of project progress payments, material supply was interrupted, production fell into semi-paralysis, and it decided to suspend all work on December 10, 2006. On March 21, 2007, Nanning City Construction Engineering Quality Inspection Center organized a comprehensive inspection of Building No. 1 Comprehensive Building, Zone A of Fortune International Plaza, Fengling Commercial Residential Community (Phase II). On May 23, 2007, Nanning City Construction Administration Department clearly stated in the minutes of the coordination meeting on the handling of the quality accident of Fortune International Plaza project that: the safety and quality problems existing in the Fortune International Plaza project constituted a major engineering quality accident. The project has been in a state of suspension since then.

During the litigation, Guiguan Company entrusted Guangxi Pusheng Real Estate Appraisal Co., Ltd. to appraise the losses arising from the price increase for repurchasing the comprehensive office building of Guiguan Company. The appraisal conclusion issued by the appraisal agency on March 2, 2008, was: The loss from the price increase for repurchasing the comprehensive office building was RMB 131,233,000. During the cross-examination, Yongcheng Company argued that the appraisal report was commissioned unilaterally by Guiguan Company, the content was not objective and fair, and claiming losses based on replacement cost had no contractual or legal basis, and there was no reason or fact for replacement. After trial and post-trial inquiries by the court of first instance, Yongcheng Company stated that it would not apply for a reappraisal commissioned by the court.

The court of first instance further found: On September 29, 2003, Yongcheng Company obtained the state-owned land use rights for four parcels of land located on the north side of Minzu Avenue, Fengling Section, Nanning City, with plot numbers 0419239, 0419211, 0419210, and 0419117, respectively. On October 9, 2003, Yongcheng Company entered into a "Maximum Amount Mortgage Contract" for RMB 100,000,000 with a commercial bank, using the land use rights of plots 0419211, 0419210, and 0419117 as collateral, and registered the mortgage on November 5, 2003, among which plot 0419210 was the land for Guiguan Company's office building.

On March 28, 2008, upon the application of Guiguan Company for preservation of property, the court of first instance, by civil ruling (2007) Gui Min Yi Chu Zi No. 2-1, lawfully sealed up the land use rights of plots 0419239 and 0419211 located on the north side of Minzu Avenue, Fengling Section, Nanning City, owned by Yongcheng Company, and the construction in progress on those two parcels of land.

On July 30, 2007, Guiguan Company filed a lawsuit, alleging: On March 12, 2003, it (Party A) entered into the "Directed Development Agreement" with Yongcheng Company (Party B), entrusting Party B to construct an office building and a commercial residential community for Party A at the Langdong Fengling Section, Nanning City. The agreement stipulated: The office building had a gross floor area of approximately 30,000 square meters and an area of approximately 30 mu; calculated at a land fee of RMB 530,000 per mu and a development and construction cost of RMB 2,500 per square meter; the residential community had an area of approximately 30 mu, with a unit price calculated at RMB 1,500 per square meter; the parties also agreed on the establishment of a joint account, payment methods, contract duration, guarantee obligations, other rights and obligations of both parties, and liability for breach of contract. After the agreement was signed, Guiguan Company actively performed the contract, but Yongcheng Company was negligent in performing its contractual obligations, and the actual construction period was greatly delayed. On March 30, 2005, the parties signed the "Supplementary Agreement," adjusting the land compensation fee from RMB 530,000 per mu to RMB 950,000 per mu, the total land compensation fee from RMB 15,900,000 to RMB 28,500,000, the basic development and construction cost from RMB 2,500 per square meter to RMB 4,350 per square meter; the office building was adjusted from 21 floors to 26 floors, and the gross floor area from 30,000 square meters to 45,955 square meters. At the same time, the parties supplemented and amended the provisions on contract duration, payment methods, and liability for breach of contract in the original Directed Development Agreement. After signing, because Yongcheng Company had multiple serious breaches of contract, including delay in construction period, substandard quality, and violation of the mortgage prohibition, which constituted a fundamental breach, the purpose of the contract could not be achieved at all, and Guiguan Company had the right to terminate the contract according to law. Guiguan Company requested the court to: 1. Terminate the "Directed Development Agreement" and the "Supplementary Agreement." 2. Order Yongcheng Company to return the investment funds already paid by Guiguan Company of RMB 110,500,000 and interest of RMB 14,760,400 (tentatively calculated as of July 30, 2007, to be calculated until the date of the judgment). 3. Order Yongcheng Company to return the deposit of RMB 1,000,000. 4. Order Yongcheng Company to bear all litigation costs of this case. On February 29, 2008, Guiguan Company added the following claims: 1. Order Yongcheng Company to pay liquidated damages for delay in construction period of RMB 51,870,000 (tentatively calculated as of July 30, 2007, to be calculated until the effective date of the judgment); 2. Order Yongcheng Company to pay liquidated damages for mortgaging the office building of RMB 50,375,900 (tentatively calculated as of July 30, 2007, to be calculated until the effective date of the judgment); 3. Order Yongcheng Company to compensate Guiguan Company for the loss of the office building project of RMB 131,233,000 (tentatively calculated as of February 29, 2008, to be calculated until the effective date of the judgment).

Yongcheng Company defended, arguing: 1. This case should be characterized as a dispute over a commercial housing sales contract. The essence of the directed development transaction was that Yongcheng Company constructed commercial housing according to Guiguan Company's requirements and delivered them to Guiguan Company, while Guiguan Company obtained commercial housing at a low price by prepaying the purchase price. According to law, the contract signed by the parties should be characterized as a commercial housing sales contract. 2. Guiguan Company delayed payment first, breaching the contract, and thus had no right to require the project to be completed on time. Although the delay in project progress was a fact, the reasons for the delay included acts caused by Guiguan Company and acts caused by the contractor, China Construction Corporation, and could not be entirely attributed to Yongcheng Company. 3. There was no irreparable quality problem in the project. 4. The land for the office building project had been taken to the Land and Resources Bureau for mortgage registration, but the Land and Resources Bureau did not process the mortgage because there was no debt relationship. Yongcheng Company did not violate the obligation prohibiting land mortgage in terms of mortgaging the land. In summary, Yongcheng Company requested the court to dismiss all of Guiguan Company's claims according to law.

The court of first instance held that, based on the parties' submissions and arguments, the issues in dispute were: 1. The nature and validity of the contract in this case. 2. Which party breached the contract in performing the contract, how the breaching party should bear liability, and whether the contract should be terminated.

Regarding the nature and validity of the contract in this case. The court of first instance held that the "Directed Development Agreement" and the "Supplementary Agreement" signed by the parties contained both elements of cooperative real estate development and clauses of construction project contracts, but the ultimate purpose of the parties was a transaction in which Guiguan Company paid the purchase price to Yongcheng Company, and Yongcheng Company delivered the ownership of the pre-agreed office complex to Guiguan Company. The substance of the rights and obligations of the parties in this transaction conformed to the essential characteristics of a house sales contract. Therefore, the contract in this case should be characterized as a dispute over a house sales contract in the name of directed base development. Yongcheng Company argued that the contract in this case should be characterized as a commercial housing sales contract. In this regard, the court of first instance held that commercial housing should be housing constructed and developed by real estate development enterprises and sold openly to the general public. The socialized and open nature of the sale is one of the characteristics of commercial housing sales. In this case, the contract signed by the parties bore the words "directed development," and the contract content stipulated that Yongcheng Company would construct an office complex for Guiguan Company, and Guiguan Company would bear all construction funds for the real estate development, and all the constructed housing would be purchased by Guiguan Company. Therefore, the target of the office building developed by Yongcheng Company in this case was specific rather than sold to the general public. Therefore, the court of first instance did not support Yongcheng Company's claim regarding the nature of a commercial housing sales contract. The court of first instance found that the "Directed Development Agreement" and the "Supplementary Agreement" signed by the parties were true expressions of the parties' intentions, did not violate the prohibitive provisions of laws and administrative regulations, and were lawful and valid contracts.

Regarding the issue of which party breached the contract during its performance, how the breaching party should bear liability, and whether the contract should be rescinded. The court of first instance held that, after Guiguan and Yongchen entered into the "Directed Development Agreement" on March 12, 2003, Guiguan paid RMB 25.9 million of the purchase price as agreed. Although Yongchen performed part of its contractual obligations, it failed to deliver the premises within the agreed time, constituting a breach of contract against Guiguan. Under these circumstances, Guiguan did not assert the right to rescind the contract or claim liability for breach of contract against Yongchen as provided in that agreement. Instead, Guiguan subsequently entered into a "Supplementary Agreement" with Yongchen on March 30, 2005. In the "Supplementary Agreement," the parties renegotiated and made new provisions regarding the office building project's area, price, payment method, construction period, guarantee obligations, other rights and obligations of the parties, and liability for breach of contract. The parties partially performed the obligations under the "Supplementary Agreement." Accordingly, it can be determined that Guiguan and Yongchen, by their conduct, showed that they substantially modified the "Directed Development Agreement" and performed the modified "Supplementary Agreement," thereby ceasing performance of the "Directed Development Agreement." Therefore, the court of first instance did not support Guiguan's claim in its lawsuit that Yongchen should bear liability for breach of contract under the "Directed Development Agreement" signed in 2003.

After the "Supplementary Agreement" was signed, Guiguan paid a total of RMB 110.5 million in purchase price to Yongchen as agreed. Yongchen failed to complete the office complex building project for Guiguan in accordance with the progress schedule stipulated in the agreement. Moreover, during the construction of Guiguan's office building, the entire Wealth International Plaza project was found by the Nanning municipal construction authority to have safety and quality issues, constituting a major project quality accident. The project was completely suspended from December 10, 2006. Yongchen was delayed in each phase of the construction period. By the contractual delivery date of February 29, 2008, the project was already impossible to actually deliver, and due to the quality accident, it still could not resume construction as of the date of judgment. As a result, the purpose of Guiguan's purchase of the office complex building could not be achieved, and Yongchen's performance constituted a fundamental breach of the contract. Pursuant to Paragraph 1 of Article 94 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China: "Under any of the following circumstances, a party may rescind the contract: ... (4) where one party delays performance of its principal obligations or commits other breaches that frustrate the purpose of the contract." Therefore, the statutory conditions for rescission of the contract were met in this case, and the court of first instance supported Guiguan's claim to rescind the contract. Yongchen argued that Guiguan's failure to pay progress payments constituted a prior breach of contract, that the contract could still be performed, and therefore disagreed with the rescission. In response, the court of first instance held that the reason the subject matter of the contract could not be delivered upon completion as agreed was the major quality accident in the Wealth International Plaza project developed by Yongchen, not Guiguan's failure to pay progress payments. Yongchen completed the construction of the fourth floor slab on December 5, 2006. According to the "Supplementary Agreement," Guiguan was obligated to pay RMB 20 million within 7 days after completion, i.e., by December 13, 2006. However, the project contractor, China State Construction Engineering Corporation, completely suspended work on December 10, 2006. Guiguan's suspension of its obligation to pay was an exercise of the right to suspend performance due to insecurity (right of defense for lack of security) and did not constitute a breach of contract. Because the project was scheduled to be delivered on February 29, 2008, but still could not resume construction due to quality issues, the court of first instance did not support Yongchen's assertion that the contract could continue to be performed.

Regarding the issue of liability after rescission of the contract, Guiguan sought in its complaint the return of the purchase price, double the deposit, payment of liquidated damages, and compensation for losses, including interest on the purchase price and the cost of replacement office building. The court of first instance held that the rescission of the contract in this case was a legal consequence arising from Yongchen's breach of contract. Rescission is not a form of liability for breach of contract, but rather a remedy after a breach. The legal consequences of rescission are not manifested as liability for breach of contract, but mainly as civil liability, including restitution of unjust enrichment and damages. Article 97 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China explicitly provides for the legal consequences after rescission: "After the rescission of a contract, for the part not yet performed, the performance shall be terminated; for the part already performed, the party may, depending on the performance situation and the nature of the contract, request restoration to the original state, take other remedial measures, and have the right to claim damages." Therefore, after rescission, Yongchen should return the purchase price of RMB 110.5 million to Guiguan and compensate Guiguan for the loss of replacement office building in the amount of RMB 131.233 million. Since the compensation for replacement cost loss was sufficient to cover Guiguan's losses, the claim for compensation for interest losses on the purchase price was not supported. Regarding the claim for double the deposit, the court of first instance held that Clause 2.3.4 of the "Supplementary Agreement" provided: "The fees paid by Guiguan before March 30, 2005 shall be considered as part of the land compensation fee already paid." Therefore, the RMB 500,000 paid by Guiguan on April 16, 2003, which had the nature of a security deposit for performance, lost its deposit nature because the "Supplementary Agreement" re-characterized it as a prepaid land payment. Moreover, the parties no longer performed the "Directed Development Agreement" but actually performed the "Supplementary Agreement," which contained no provisions regarding a deposit. Therefore, the court of first instance did not support Guiguan's claim for double the deposit. Regarding Guiguan's claim for liquidated damages for delay in construction period and unauthorized mortgage of land by Yongchen, the court of first instance held that the contract in this case was essentially a contract for the sale of real property. The provisions in the contract regarding the construction period and land mortgage were inconsistent with the characteristics of a real estate sale contract. Moreover, pursuant to Article 97 of the Contract Law, the legal effect of rescission is to extinguish the contractual relationship. As a consequence of rescission, the breaching party's liability does not take the form of liquidated damages. Therefore, the court of first instance also did not support Guiguan's claim for liquidated damages. As for Yongchen's defense that Guiguan did not actually purchase a replacement office building and therefore suffered no actual loss, that the replacement cost loss did not exist, and that the loss appraisal report was commissioned unilaterally by Guiguan and could not be used as evidence of loss, the court of first instance held that it was a fact that Guiguan had not actually purchased a replacement office building. The reason Guiguan did not purchase one was that RMB 110.5 million of the purchase price had already been invested in this project. To require Guiguan to invest a large sum of additional funds to purchase a comparable office building in order to be compensated for losses would be excessively harsh and unfair to Guiguan. After two rounds of evidence exchange and questioning at trial, Yongchen only disputed the result of the appraisal report without providing contrary evidence, and explicitly stated that it would not apply to the court to commission a new appraisal, thereby waiving its litigation rights. Even if the loss conclusion in the appraisal report differed from the actual loss, the adverse legal consequences should be borne by Yongchen. Therefore, the court of first instance did not accept Yongchen's defense against compensation.

In summary, the court of first instance found that the contract in this case, though named a base directed development agreement, was essentially a dispute over a real estate sale contract. Yongchen fundamentally breached the contract during performance. Guiguan's claim for rescission, return of the purchase price, and compensation for replacement office building losses had merit and was supported by the court. Yongchen's allegation that Guiguan breached the contract first and that the contract could continue to be performed was inconsistent with the facts and was not accepted. Pursuant to Article 94 and Article 97 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China and Article 128 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, following deliberation by the adjudication committee of the court of first instance, the judgment was rendered as follows: 1. Rescind the "Directed Development Agreement" and the "Supplementary Agreement" entered into between Guiguan and Yongchen; 2. Yongchen shall return to Guiguan the purchase price of RMB 110,500,000; 3. Yongchen shall compensate Guiguan for losses in the amount of RMB 131,233,000; 4. Dismiss Guiguan's other claims. The case acceptance fee of RMB 1,840,496 and the litigation preservation fee of RMB 5,000, totaling RMB 1,845,496, shall be borne by Yongchen in the amount of RMB 1,107,297.6 and by Guiguan in the amount of RMB 738,198.4.

Yongchen, dissatisfied with the judgment of the court of first instance, appealed to this Court, arguing that the facts found by the court of first instance were erroneous; the "Directed Development Agreement" and "Supplementary Agreement" signed by the parties were not a commercial housing sale contract; the contracts involved were invalid because Guiguan knew before signing that Yongchen had not obtained the pre-sale permit for the commercial housing; Yongchen's failure to pay the project progress payment was an exercise of the right to suspend performance due to insecurity; the finding by the court of first instance that Yongchen fundamentally breached the contract was factually erroneous; the determination that Yongchen should compensate Guiguan RMB 131,233,000 had no factual basis; and the court of first instance omitted a necessary party and violated statutory procedure.

Guiguan argued in its defense that the facts found and the law applied by the court of first instance were correct and should be affirmed.

This Court, upon further fact-finding on appeal, found that the project involved had still not obtained a commercial housing pre-sale permit as of the date of the appellate trial.

Other facts found by this Court on appeal were the same as those found by the court of first instance.

This Court holds that the issues in dispute between the parties are: the validity of the contracts involved, whether the contracts should be rescinded, and, if rescinded, how the consequences should be handled.

Regarding the validity of the contracts involved. Based on the facts of this case, on March 12, 2003, Guiguan (Party A) and Yongchen (Party B) entered into the "Directed Development Agreement," by which Guiguan commissioned Yongchen to construct an office complex and a commercial residential community for Guiguan at the Langdong Fengling section of Nanning, Guangxi. The agreement provided: the main office building was initially planned to be 21 stories, covering approximately 30 mu of land, with a floor area of approximately 30,000 square meters. The total investment in the office building included: land at RMB 530,000 per mu (including land leveling costs); the development and construction cost was tentatively calculated at RMB 2,500 per square meter of floor area. The commercial residential community was to be a 6-story frame structure, covering approximately 30 mu of land, with a unit price calculated at RMB 1,500 per square meter. The parties also made provisions regarding joint escrow accounts, payment methods, contract period, guarantee obligations, other rights and obligations of the parties, and liability for breach of contract. From the agreement of the parties, the "Directed Development Agreement" signed by the parties reflected their true intentions, did not violate prohibitive provisions of law, and should be a valid contract.

Regarding whether the contracts should be rescinded and how to handle the consequences after rescission. The parties stipulated the following regarding the project period and delivery: the project shall be completed and accepted within 28 months from the start of main construction, and delivered for Guiguan's use within 2 months after passing the acceptance inspection. Regarding rights and obligations, the parties agreed: Guiguan has the right to supervise the progress of the project, and if the physical progress does not meet the planned requirements, Guiguan has the right to refuse to make any payment. Regarding delivery, it was agreed: if Yongchen cannot deliver on time, Guiguan may choose to notify Yongchen to rescind the agreement or continue to wait. If Guiguan chooses to continue waiting, the waiting period shall be determined by Guiguan, and Guiguan may still rescind the agreement after waiting. Based on the facts of this case, Yongchen did not complete the project on time, and under the terms of the parties' agreement, Guiguan is entitled to rescind the contract.

Regarding the issue of liability after rescission of the contract, Guiguan sought in its complaint the return of the purchase price, double the deposit, payment of liquidated damages, and compensation for losses, including interest on the purchase price and the cost of replacement office building. This Court holds that, pursuant to Article 97 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China: "After the rescission of a contract, for the part not yet performed, the performance shall be terminated; for the part already performed, the party may, depending on the performance situation and the nature of the contract, request restoration to the original state, take other remedial measures, and have the right to claim damages." Therefore, after rescission, Yongchen should return the purchase price and interest to Guiguan. Regarding Guiguan's claim for double the deposit, Clause 2.3.4 of the "Supplementary Agreement" provided: "The fees paid by Guiguan before March 30, 2005 shall be considered as part of the land compensation fee already paid." Therefore, the RMB 500,000 paid by Guiguan on April 16, 2003, which had the nature of a performance deposit, lost its deposit nature because the "Supplementary Agreement" re-characterized it as a prepaid land payment. Accordingly, it shall not be returned. Regarding Guiguan's claim for liquidated damages for delay in construction period and unauthorized mortgage of land by Yongchen, this Court holds that the legal effect of rescission is to extinguish the contractual relationship. As a consequence of rescission, the breaching party's liability does not take the form of liquidated damages. Therefore, this Court also does not support Guiguan's claim for liquidated damages. Given that after the rescission of the contract, Guiguan will need to incur expenses to purchase a replacement office building, and that Yongchen constructed the office and residential buildings specifically for Guiguan's requirements, the non-performance of the contract will also cause certain losses to Yongchen. Considering the actual circumstances of this case as a whole, this Court determines in its discretion that Yongchen shall compensate Guiguan for losses in the amount of RMB 10,000,000. Pursuant to Subparagraph (3) of Paragraph 1 of Article 153 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the judgment is as follows:

1. Affirm Items 1 and 4 of the Civil Judgment (2007) Gui Min Yi Chu Zi No. 2 of the High People's Court of Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region;

2. Amend Item 2 of the Civil Judgment (2007) Gui Min Yi Chu Zi No. 2 of the High People's Court of Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region to: Guangxi Yongchen Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. shall, within three months after this judgment takes effect, return RMB 110,500,000 to Guiguan, and pay interest on each payment at the same period's benchmark lending rate of the People's Bank of China from the day following receipt of each payment until the day of actual payment;

3. Amend Item 3 of the Civil Judgment (2007) Gui Min Yi Chu Zi No. 2 of the High People's Court of Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region to: Guangxi Yongchen Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. shall compensate Guangxi Guiguan Electric Power Co., Ltd. for losses in the amount of RMB 10,000,000.

If the obligation to pay money is not fulfilled within the period specified in this judgment, interest on the debt for delayed performance shall be paid in double pursuant to Article 229 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China.

The court acceptance fee for the first instance and the litigation preservation fee total RMB 1,845,496, which shall be borne by Guangxi Guiguan Electric Power Co., Ltd. in the amount of RMB 1,107,297.6 and by Guangxi Yongchen Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. in the amount of RMB 738,198.4; the court acceptance fee for the second instance is RMB 967,965, which shall be borne by Guangxi Guiguan Electric Power Co., Ltd. in the amount of RMB 677,575.5 and by Guangxi Yongchen Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. in the amount of RMB 290,389.5.
